_doc: M1-CHR-15: how the heroes' helper bones follow a pose. assets_src/characters/asha/hero_clips.py bakes them into every clip from these values; game/characters/hero_helper_bones.gd solves the same for poses set outside a clip (the character stages' world_pose, cutscene placeholder poses). The builds add the bones (assets_src/characters/asha/helper_bones.py); a skeleton without them is left alone.
_key_tolerance_doc: hero_clips.py drops a baked helper-bone key that the slerp between its neighbouring kept keys reproduces within this many degrees (the runtime solve itself matches the bake within 1 degree).

armpit._doc: DEF-armpit.L/.R sit on the shoulder with the upper arm's head, tail and roll, and turn `share` of the upper arm's own turn (relative to the shoulder) while the arm comes down, rising to all of it as the arm lifts above its rest elevation by raise_full_deg (the arm's own lift, in the skeleton's frame): the underarm skin rides them, so a lowered arm does not sink into the torso cloth, and a raised one carries it as before.

skirt._doc: DEF-skirt_<k> (pivot on the outer skirt above the hip joints, down to the panels' first joint at mid-thigh), DEF-skirt_<k>.001 (on to just below the knee) and DEF-skirt_<k>.002 (on to the hem; M2-CHR-522), the `levels` suffixes from the hips down: one chain per sector of the floor-length skirts, parented to the hips. Each bone swings out in the vertical plane through its sector by the least angle from the vertical (coarse steps of grid_deg, then `bisect` halvings, up to max_swing_deg) that keeps every vertex of `cloth_mesh` with at least cloth_min_weight on it within slack_m of its rest distance (capped at clear_m) from the axis of every leg segment (both legs). The bones are solved from the hips down, each about its head where the bones above put it, so the bone below the knee hangs back towards the vertical once its cloth clears the shin; at each level neighbouring panels may not lag each other by more than lag_deg_per_45 per 45 degrees between them. Floor-length cloth that cannot hang its full length (kneeling, crouching) pools: where the lowest bone's cloth would pass floor_clear_m above the floor (the skeleton's y = 0), the lowest bone takes a scale along its length (the gather, down to gather_min, found by `bisect` halvings) and 1 + gather_flare * (1 - gather) across it, baked as scale_3d keys. Where that gather would fall below drape_below_gather (pooling, not a walk's lifted hem), the lowest bone first swings out onto the floor: the least swing, up to drape_max_deg, at which its full cloth stays floor_clear_m above the floor, so pooled cloth spreads instead of being crushed into a wall. ADR 0140: the even-numbered panels are derived, not baked (the odd ones lie over the legs at rest, so they are solved): each takes the larger of its two odd neighbours' swings (their mean cut into a thigh between them; at the hem, though, their mean, since the larger folded it into spikes) and the mean of their gathers, and its lowest bone swings fold_deg further out, eased in over fold_ease_deg once that swing lies past fold_from_deg (cloth draped out on the floor), so a pooled hem folds. HeroSkirtFolds (a SkeletonModifier3D the characters import adds) does it every frame from the odd panels' pose; hero_clips.derive_folds is the same rule offline. A lowest bone swung out past overhang_from_deg lies over the legs, and the cloth that would run on past them falls: it gathers to end overhang_margin_m past the farthest leg point (sampled at support_samples + 1 points per segment) within support_lateral_m of the panel's plane, eased in over overhang_ease_deg of swing.
